sl.eyebrow: Alliance vs alliance · every two weeks
sl.title: Swordland Showdown
sl.thesis: Two alliances, one map, {minutes} minutes. It is not won by whoever is biggest. It is won by whoever knows their job before the whistle.
sl.roster.title: Who takes the field
sl.roster.lede: A Legion is {mains} main fighters plus {subs} substitutes. Only the top {top} alliances by power can register at all, so a seat is never guaranteed just because you signed up.
sl.roster.subs: Main slots nobody claims open to the {subs} substitutes {n} minutes into the match, first come first served. If you are a substitute, be online at the start anyway.
sl.legions.head: An alliance can register {n} Legions.
sl.legions.body: Alliance rewards follow Legion 1's result and nothing else. Legion 2 can win its own match and it does not change the alliance payout.
sl.legions.do: Legion 1 takes the stronger accounts. Take a Legion 2 seat anyway — personal rewards follow your own Relic Point rank in either one.
sl.teams.title: Three teams
sl.teams.lede: Every Legion splits its {mains} into three groups. Know which one you are in before the match starts, because there is no time to ask during it.
sl.teams.note: The thirds are a shape, not a rule. A Legion short on heavy accounts runs fewer attackers and a bigger garrison. What matters is that all {mains} know which group they are in.
team.attack.name: Attackers
team.attack.duty: The heaviest accounts. Contest the Sanctums early and the Swordshrine late, and spend troops hitting enemy players and taking buildings rather than sitting on a structure. Killing pays about {payRatio}× on offence — roughly {attackPay} Relic Points per 10,000 enemy power defeated, against {defendPay} defending.
team.attack.note: Attackers reinforce nobody. You are the ones being reinforced, and your job is to attack.
team.jump.name: Jumpers
team.jump.duty: Mid-power accounts that never stand still. Split across the map to flip Abbeys, chase Undercellar waves as they arrive, and pick up Baggage Trains. With the Royal Stables held your teleport is back in {tpFast} minutes, so keep moving.
team.jump.note: Jumpers quietly score the most personal points, because they are never waiting for anything.
team.support.name: Garrison
team.support.duty: Garrison the buildings the attackers take, and join long-range rallies. When attackers' and jumpers' troops drop low and leave to heal for {heal} minutes, garrison members may be called to replace them.
team.support.note: Only hold what we can defend. It is better to focus on holding strategic buildings than to defend everything, and it is fine to abandon a building we cannot hold — especially one with few points accumulated on it, since the first capture is already banked.
sl.rot.title: The rotation
sl.rot.body: Troops do not last an hour. When the attackers run low they retreat and heal, and that takes {heal} minutes — long enough that a Legion with no plan simply stops scoring for a quarter of the match.
sl.rot.head: Healing is a {heal} minute hole in your line.
sl.rot.why: If the attackers and the garrison go low at the same time, both are in the infirmary together and the map flips while you wait.
sl.rot.do: Stagger it. Attackers heal first while the garrison does the attacking, then swap back the moment the attackers are whole again. Nobody heals on their own initiative.
sl.phases.title: How the hour runs
sl.phases.lede: {minutes} minutes, three phases. Each one puts something new on the map, and the new thing is always worth more than what came before.
sl.phases.warn: Only the wave times are still unread. Everything else here comes off the match itself.
phase.one.title: Take the cheap ground
phase.one.body: Sanctums, Abbeys, the Bell Tower and the Royal Stables are all open. Our main targets are {targets}. The Stables cut every teleport that follows from {tp} minutes to {tpFast}, worth more than the points on any single building, and the Sanctums are the steady flow the lead gets built on. Abbeys and the Bell Tower get picked up around them.
phase.two.title: The Swordshrine and the Hall open
phase.two.body: The Swordshrine, the Hall of Reformation and the Mercenary Camp unlock together. Take the Hall — it raises the combat power everything after it is fought with. The Shrine is the biggest point source on the map and it is under constant mercenary attack, so holding it this early usually means handing it straight back. Its first capture is still a one-off worth grabbing, and you keep that even when you lose the building.
phase.three.title: Undercellar waves
phase.three.body: Undercellars arrive in {waves} waves and pay out for plain gathering, with no fight required. The jumpers live on these. The Swordshrine push still waits for the last {n} minutes.
sl.shrine.head: Do not commit to the Swordshrine before the last {n} minutes.
sl.shrine.body: When a building flips, {pct}% of the alliance points banked on it are still sitting there for whoever takes it. Hold the Shrine early and you are storing points for the enemy to collect.
sl.shrine.do: Build the lead on Sanctums and Abbeys. Take the Shrine with {n} minutes left, and hold it to the whistle.
sl.points.title: Worth knowing
sl.points.q: Should I defend a building or go and hit someone?
sl.points.a: Hit someone. Defeating enemy troops pays about {attackPay} Relic Points per 10,000 power on offence against about {defendPay} defending — roughly {payRatio}× for the same troops. Defend only while the building is actually generating for you.
sl.first.title: First capture pays once
sl.first.lede: The first alliance to fully occupy a building, once its capture timer completes, takes the one-time bonus in the table above — in both alliance and personal points. It is paid once per building for the whole match, and then it is gone for everyone.
sl.first.head: A first capture cannot be taken back.
sl.first.body: Occupation points bank on the building, and {pct}% of them are still sitting there for whoever flips it next. The first-capture bonus does not work that way. It pays the moment the building becomes yours and it stays paid even if you lose the building a minute later.
sl.first.do: At the whistle, spread out and claim uncontested buildings instead of stacking on one. Every building nobody has taken yet is a bonus still on the table, and with four of them the Abbeys are the easiest first captures on the map.
bonus.weaken: Weakens attack and defence on enemy garrisons
sl.pay.title: What every building pays
sl.pay.lede: Two numbers per building: the one-time bonus for taking it first, then the rate it pays every minute you keep it. Alliance and personal points are counted separately and you earn both at the same time.
sl.pay.note: Four Abbeys, two Sanctums, one of everything else.
sl.pay.head: Both Sanctums beat the Swordshrine — {bothSanctums} a minute against {shrineRate}.
sl.pay.body: The Shrine is the richest single building on the map, but there is only one of it. Two Sanctums pay {bothSanctums} alliance points a minute between them, against the Shrine's {shrineRate}, and they are open from the whistle instead of a quarter of an hour in.
sl.pay.do: Hold both Sanctums before anyone argues about the Shrine. The Bell Tower and Royal Stables are worth taking for their effects rather than their points — they are the cheapest buildings on the board.
sl.first.egq: Is the Swordshrine worth taking if we cannot hold it?
sl.first.ega: Yes. Being first into the Shrine pays {shrineFirst} to the alliance and {shrineFirstYou} to you, and you keep every point of that even if you lose it thirty seconds later. Holding it is what pays {shrineRate} a minute, and that is the part worth fighting for in the last {n} minutes.
sl.lock.title: The first {n} minutes
sl.lock.lede: Joining does not let you act. The map is locked for about {n} minutes. Use it to send reinforcements.
sl.lock.head: Garrison and jumpers each reinforce {m} attackers.
sl.lock.body: Attackers send nothing — they spend the window lining up what they hit first. Everyone else does the reinforcing. One march per player, so that is {m} different names.
sl.lock.do: Send both before the clock releases, and spread them across the squad — if everyone reinforces the same {m} players, the rest of the attack team is undefended. Watch chat for who still needs cover.
sl.go.title: Game on
sl.go.lede: The lock lifts and everything happens at once. This is the order it happens in.
go.teleport.title: Only the attackers teleport
go.teleport.body: Jumpers and the garrison stay exactly where they are. One squad goes onto the map, and it is the one built to fight for a building.
go.insurance.title: Jumpers and garrison start {n} rallies each
go.insurance.body: On the nearest Sanctum and on the Abbeys. These are insurance: if the attackers cannot take a building outright, a rally is already running on it and nothing is lost waiting to start one.
go.take.title: Attackers take the Sanctums and the Bell Tower
go.take.body: The Sanctums are the richest thing open at the whistle and the Bell Tower cuts capture time on everything that follows. Both are worth an attacker's first move.
go.garrison.title: Garrison and jumpers march into what is taken
go.garrison.body: A garrison march into a captured building releases the attacker sitting on it. An attacker parked on a Sanctum is an attacker not taking the next thing.
go.move.title: Attackers move on to the Stables and the Abbeys
go.move.body: Freed up, they go for the Royal Stables and then work through the Abbeys, taking each one first rather than settling on it.
sl.go.head: We are farming first captures, not holding ground.
sl.go.body: There are four Abbeys and we do not need to keep any of them. Every building we touch first pays its one-time bonus, and that bonus stays ours whatever happens to the building a minute later.
sl.go.do: Once the first captures are banked, the Bell Tower stops mattering — its bonus was for the captures. Pull those troops out and put them into Abbeys.
sl.cycle.title: The target cycle
sl.cycle.lede: With the first captures banked, the rest of the match is one loop, run over and over until the whistle.
cyc.wait.title: Let their points build
cyc.wait.body: A building pays its owner every minute, and {pct}% of everything it has banked is still sitting on it. The longer they hold it, the more there is on it to take. Patience is the whole move here.
cyc.mark.title: An R4 marks the target
cyc.mark.body: The next building to hit gets a bookmark labelled “{mark}”. That bookmark is the signal — when one appears, jumpers get ready.
cyc.jump.title: Chat calls the jump
cyc.jump.body: Jumpers teleport in and surround the building, staying a safe distance from it. Surrounding is not about the attack. It is about what happens the moment the building falls.
cyc.rally.title: An attacker calls a {n} minute rally
cyc.rally.body: Every jumper joins it. One short rally with the whole squad in it, and the building comes down before the other side can reinforce it properly.
cyc.grab.title: Grab the relics
cyc.grab.body: When the building falls, the relics scatter in every direction. Standing spread around it is what puts somebody near each one. That is why you surround the building instead of stacking on one side of it.
sl.cycle.repeat: Then mark the next target and run it again.
sl.cycle.head: Surround first, rally second.
sl.cycle.body: A squad stacked on one side of a building takes it just as well and then watches half the relics land out of reach. The spread is the part that pays.
sl.cycle.do: Keep a safe distance while you wait. Close enough to reach the relics, far enough that you are not picked off standing still before the rally lands.
sl.shrine.title: The Swordshrine
sl.lock.targets.head: Attackers pick their targets.
sl.lock.targets.body: The Sanctums and the Bell Tower are the focus. Past those, try for as many other first rewards as possible — every building we reach first pays once, whether we hold it or not.
squads.title: Who is in which squad
squads.lede: Two Legions, three squads each. Find your face, and read the duty for that squad above.
squads.note: Alliance rewards follow Legion 1's result, so Legion 1 carries the heavier accounts. Personal rewards follow your own Relic Point rank in either one.
